notes.text: Justin Holl has not dressed for the last 7 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Jack St. Ivany has taken his spot beside Cole Hutson. That pair has had 60% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 50:51 together.

Rasmus Sandin is on long-term injured reserve (knee surgery) and has missed the last 11 games. He is a top-four defenseman. Timothy Liljegren has taken his spot beside Martin Fehérváry. That pair has had 48% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 67:53 together.
Jack St. Ivany is no longer killing penalties: 4% of the team’s shorthanded time in 5 games, down from 35% with his old team last season.
Jakob Chychrun has started killing penalties: on the ice for 27% of the team’s shorthanded time in 15 games, up from 8% last season.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 26% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the fourth-lowest in the league (a typical team: 40%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
William Eklund is out 10-12 weeks and has missed the last 14 games.

story.head: Who’s in net for the Senators?
paras: The Senators have won two in a row, and the Capitals (9-6-0) beat Florida 4-3 on Saturday. Going in, the Caps are fourth in the Metropolitan (tied for 19th in the NHL) and the Senators fourth in the Atlantic (ninth).
The Capitals’ record (.600) is about what their chances are worth. The Senators’ record (.639) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.570), largely because they’re 5-1 in one-goal games.

The Capitals have had some of the best goaltending in the league (4th), but give up a lot of dangerous shots (28th). They also get the league’s best looks (1st), so their good looks will be harder to come by against the Senators. The Senators rarely get pinned in their own end (2nd) and play slow, tight games (3rd lowest). They also are one of the league’s most physical teams (3rd), so the Senators have the edge over the Capitals on physicality.

Jordan Kyrou (5 G / 9 A / 14 P in 15 GP) leads the Capitals in scoring, and Alex Tuch (11 G / 2 A / 13 P in 15 GP) has a team-high eleven goals, tied for sixth in the NHL. For the Senators, Tim Stützle (9 G / 14 A / 23 P in 18 GP) leads the way in scoring, with seven points in his last five games and a point in five straight games against Washington. Drake Batherson (9 G / 9 A / 18 P in 18 GP) is next in line.
Logan Thompson (6-4-0 / .889 SV% in 11 GS) will likely start for Washington, and Samuel Ersson (3-3-1 / .889 SV% in 6 GS) for Ottawa.
